authorship: Hand-authored notification and projection witnesses over docs/X1_TRANSPORT_CONTRACT.md section 9 and the A0 acceptance law (generation newer, or equal generation with strictly greater sequence; matching request/document/revision identities). No production transport code exists or was consulted.

cases.title: Exactly one notification per settled status change

expected.law: Each admitted status-changing command publishes exactly one notification after it settles; refusals and no-op receipts publish none.

cases.title: Sequence strictly increases across the lifetime

expected.law: notificationSequence is a positive safe integer strictly greater than every previously published sequence regardless of generation; a (generation, sequence) pair is never reused or decreased.

cases.title: Stop-then-stale-playhead rejection at the boundary
cases.scenario: A playing-status notification carrying generation G is delivered to the application after Stop already published ready at generation G+1.

expected.law: The service publishes in admission order, so the stale delivery can only exist through transport-layer reordering; the A0 acceptance law rejects it and an old playhead cannot repaint after Stop. This is the stale transport-view regression witness.

cases.title: Interruption publishes paused with the stable code

expected.law: The interrupted state projects to paused plus the frozen failure code so the application can render an actionable recovery affordance without a new status.
One failed notification carries a stable transport or engine code; repeated faults inside one fault state publish nothing further.

cases.title: Replacement rebinds identity fields
cases.scenario: replace-plan installs documentId d2 planRevision 9 after playing d1 revision 4.

expected.law: The replacement notification carries the new identities; the application's matching rule makes any late d1 notification stale by identity, not just by sequence.

cases.title: Playhead field is the exact settled beat

expected.law: Notifications carry exact rational beats computed from the epoch anchor, never interpolated display positions.

cases.title: Sequence exhaustion is terminal, not wrapping
cases.scenario: The next sequence would exceed the maximum safe integer.

expected.law: Sequences never wrap; exhaustion refuses the command or faults the service with the stable code.
